title: Scan every pair, then color the edges
coverageNote: One supplied result and one primary source, reviewed as a full-output baseline. This is not an exhaustive matrix-query frontier.
lowerBoundStatus: No matrix-query lower bound is verified in the supplied source set. No optimality claim is made.

verifiedRecords.output: Explicit proper coloring of every edge: m edge–color assignments.
verifiedRecords.graph: Undirected simple graph on a known n-vertex set; m edges, maximum degree Δ.
verifiedRecords.oracle: Pair(u,v) returns one adjacency bit. No neighbor list, degree query, sampling oracle or supplied edge list.
verifiedRecords.postScanTime: O(m log Δ) w.h.p. for Δ≥2
verifiedRecords.theorem: Corollary C.1(1), with proof in §C.1; deterministic matrix enumeration is an atlas derivation.
verifiedRecords.probability: Enumeration uses exactly n(n−1)/2 queries deterministically. The static coloring stage produces a proper (Δ+1)-edge coloring within O(m log Δ) time with high probability in n, for Δ≥2. No fixed failure exponent is imposed here.
assumptions: Known vertex set; one unit-cost Pair(u,v) query returns adjacency in a fixed undirected simple graph.
Query every unordered pair u<v once; build a stored graph and compute its maximum degree during the scan.
All actual edges are retained before the randomized static coloring stage; that stage makes no additional matrix-oracle queries.
Explicit output includes a color for every actual edge; absent pairs are not output.
For Δ=0 output is empty; for Δ=1 assign color 1 to each edge in O(m) additional time. The expression log max{2,Δ} extends the displayed time to these trivial cases.
verifiedRecords.notes: The exact matrix-query count is the cost of this full-scan construction, not a matrix-oracle theorem of the cited paper. The same scan runs on sparse and dense graphs. Theorem 1.1 states O(m log n); the sharper degree-sensitive time comes from Corollary C.1(1). The total time includes enumeration. No query lower bound or oracle optimality is claimed.
derivation: There are exactly C(n,2)=n(n−1)/2 unordered vertex pairs.
Query each pair once. The returned bits determine the full simple graph; retain its m actual edges and compute Δ.
Apply Corollary C.1(1) to the stored graph for Δ≥2; handle Δ≤1 directly.
Emit the m edge–color assignments. Enumeration and output are counted separately from the static coloring theorem.
verifiedRecords.kindExplanation: Algorithm baseline; exact query accounting, not a lower bound.

y.label: Pair queries · symbolic asymptotic order
y.note: Ordered asymptotic reference tiers only; the point is Θ(n²), annotated with exact n(n−1)/2. This is not a numeric interpolation or a second result.

sourceVerification.theorem: Corollary C.1(1); Theorem 1.1; Appendix C.1 proof
sourceVerification.notes: Corollary C.1(1) gives O(m log Δ) randomized computation w.h.p. for a simple graph. Theorem 1.1 gives O(m log n), so the main-theorem citation was sharpened. Exact pair-query enumeration is an elementary atlas composition, independently checked. Δ≤1 handled explicitly.

composition.storageNote: O(m) retained edges; no total-memory claim for the static coloring algorithm.
composition.sparseDense: The scan is identical on sparse and dense inputs.
